pension.title: Social Security pension
pension.intro: Optional income from your pension age. Prefer the net amount from the official Social Security simulator, adjusted for stopping work at FIRE.
pension.ageNote: The normal pension age is 66 years and 9 months in 2026, and 66 years and 11 months in 2027. Your future pension age is an editable assumption. Annual pension payments are spread across monthly spending.
pension.estimateNote: Approximation for the general post-2002 regime: future service stops at FIRE, at least 15 contribution years are needed and at most 40 are counted. Future salary stays constant in real terms; career-average pay should already be revalued into today's euros. For pre-2002 careers, early retirement or special regimes, enter an official estimate.
pension.projected: Future pension: {amount} net/year from age {age}, in today's euros.

risk.title: Monte Carlo assumptions
risk.note: FIRE is the earliest retirement date meeting your success target. Independent yearly lognormal returns vary; growth is spread evenly within each year and inflation is fixed. Simulated success is not a guarantee. Contributions stop at FIRE.
risk.resultNote: Target {target} · {count} simulated paths. Success means funding every retirement expense through the planning horizon.
risk.chartNote: The line is the median portfolio, with a 10th–90th percentile band. Percentiles at each age are not a single investment path. The constant-return reference does not determine FIRE.

life_expectancy.text: The simulated plan must fund all retirement spending through this age. A longer horizon also tests living longer than expected.

desired_monthly_net_income.text: Total monthly spending after tax in today's euros. Pension income covers part of this amount once it starts; investments fund the rest.

initial_balance.text: Starting balance in today’s euros. The model assumes this value has no prior gains to be taxed.

monthly_contribution.text: Monthly amount invested before FIRE, in each year's euros. Contributions stop at FIRE. It only rises if you set an annual raise.

contribution_growth_rate.text: Annual increase rate to contributions in each year’s euros. 0% = no raise; inflation rate = constant purchasing power.

annual_roi.text: Expected arithmetic annual return before inflation and fees. Simulated returns vary with volatility; this return is not earned every year.

inflation_rate.text: Expected annual raise in prices. Converts between each year's euros and today's euros; also used for the Real / Nominal toggle.

management_fee_rate.text: Annual funds and platform costs (TER, management, custody, etc.). Excludes buy/sell and other trading commissions.

gains_tax_rate.text: Capital gains tax rate on profits when you sell your investments. Oldest holdings are assumed to be sold first (FIFO).

warning.title: These values cannot be used
warning.wholeNumber: {field} must be a whole number from {min} to {max}.
warning.ageOrder: Current Age must be less than Life Expectancy.
warning.contributionYears: Contribution years cannot exceed years since age 16.
warning.calculate: Could not calculate with these inputs.

coast.hint: Coast FIRE is reached when you can stop investing and still reach FIRE at the legal retirement age. Yellow line shows the growth trajectory from that point until FIRE.

units.hint:
Real values are amounts in today’s euros — future values are deflated to today's purchasing power.

Nominal values are amounts in each year’s euros — future values are shown as on that year's account statement.

table.title: Year-by-year
table.noteReal: All amounts in real values (i.e. in today's euros).
table.noteNominal: All amounts in nominal values (i.e. in each year's euros).

chart.congrats: Planned retirement meets the simulated success target.
chart.insideRegion: After planned retirement; investment outcomes vary.

footer.disclaimerIntro: FIRE Calculator © is provided for educational and simulation purposes only. All figures are illustrative projections based on the inputs provided by the user and on the assumptions built into the model. They are not a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any asset, and they do not constitute financial, investment, tax, legal, or retirement advice.
footer.disclaimerLimitations: Monte Carlo uses independent yearly lognormal returns and fixed inflation. Results have sampling uncertainty and depend on return, volatility, longevity and pension assumptions. Correlations, changing inflation, future laws, progressive tax elections and special tax regimes are not fully represented. Capital gains use a flat tax on positive FIFO nominal gains. Initial capital is assumed to have no prior unrealised gains. Pension estimates are simplified; use the official simulator for your circumstances. No success rate guarantees retirement income.
